name: millennial-optimism-loft
prompt: A tall portrait photograph of an empty converted warehouse flat on a golden late afternoon, nobody in it, shot from a low corner of the room at roughly waist height with a slightly wide lens so the old brick walls lean in a little and the ceiling beams run away overhead. Big multi-pane steel-framed industrial windows fill the back wall and pour thick honey-coloured sun across scuffed wide floorboards, with dust hanging in the beams. Bare amber filament bulbs dangle on long black cords from the rafters and a loose string of warm fairy lights is looped along the exposed brick. In the foreground, a low coffee table made of rough salvaged planks holds a glass preserving jar stuffed with daisies and cornflowers, a jar with tea lights inside, a mug printed with a tiny repeating curled-moustache pattern, and a stack of unmarked vinyl sleeves. Behind it a cracked tan leather sofa with a knitted throw and a small ukulele resting against one arm. A turntable sits on a crate in the midground with its lid up. By the door, a skinny single-speed bicycle with a mint-green frame leans against the brick. One wall is painted matte blackboard black and wiped completely clean. The whole frame is graded like a phone snapshot from 2012 run through a faded vintage filter: lifted milky blacks, creamy yellow-beige highlights, slightly washed mint and peach midtones, gentle soft focus at the edges and a soft dark vignette in the corners. Hopeful, cosy and a touch smug, the feeling of a cheap first flat when everything was going to work out. No text, no lettering, no logos anywhere. Thanks.
